skill.name: swiftui-expert-skill
skill.description: Create, review, modernize, and profile SwiftUI code for iOS and macOS using focused guidance and Instruments trace analysis.
skill.summary: Improve SwiftUI correctness, accessibility, performance, and API adoption with targeted references and trace tooling.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 278 static findings are false positives caused by Swift syntax, Markdown backticks, documentation examples, or fixed xctrace argument-array subprocess calls. No prompt injection, runtime network request, private-key access, environment-file read, or shell interpolation was found. One high-severity semantic issue remains because launch environment values are printed without redaction.

remediation.issue: The recording helper prints complete --env KEY=VALUE arguments, which can expose credentials in terminal or agent logs.
remediation.suggestion: Redact each --env value before printing the command, and document that sensitive values should not appear in captured logs.

content.value_statement: SwiftUI defects often hide in state flow, identity, layout, and invalidation behavior. This skill provides focused reviews, modern patterns, and Instruments-based diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SwiftUI state ownership, bindings, observable models, environment use, and data flow.
Refactors view composition, list identity, layout, navigation, focus, animation, and accessibility patterns.
Identifies deprecated SwiftUI APIs and proposes availability-gated replacements with fallbacks.
Provides guidance for localization, image optimization, previews, charts, and macOS-specific views.
Records Instruments traces through xctrace for selected apps, devices, or system-wide sessions.
Analyzes trace lanes for hangs, hitches, hot symbols, SwiftUI updates, and invalidation causes.
limitations: Trace recording requires macOS, Xcode, xctrace, and access to the selected process or device.
The SwiftUI Instruments lane is unavailable for iOS Simulator recordings.
Version-specific recommendations depend on the installed SDK and require project-level verification.
Guidance does not replace builds, tests, accessibility audits, or device validation.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing Screen
use_cases.description: Replace deprecated APIs, correct state ownership, and add availability fallbacks without imposing a new architecture.

use_cases.title: Review a SwiftUI Change
use_cases.description: Check identity, view composition, accessibility, localization, and performance risks before merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Runtime Hitches
use_cases.description: Record or inspect an Instruments trace and prioritize expensive views, blocked intervals, and invalidation sources.

prompt_templates.title: Review a View
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for state, identity, accessibility, and deprecated APIs. Explain the highest-impact fixes first.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused code review.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement this SwiftUI feature for the stated deployment targets. Design data flow first and include availability fallbacks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs production-ready SwiftUI guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these SwiftUI views to reduce invalidations and expensive body work. Preserve behavior and identify measurable verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team sees slow updates or scrolling.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Instruments Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Instruments trace within the requested time window. Correlate hangs, hitches, hot symbols, and SwiftUI invalidation causes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs evidence-based performance diagnosis.

output_examples.input: Review a settings form that stores an injected model as local state.
output_examples.output: The review identifies incorrect ownership, recommends observable injection, checks binding scope, and lists targeted validation steps.

output_examples.input: Modernize a navigation flow while supporting older deployment targets.
output_examples.output: The response proposes current navigation APIs, marks availability boundaries, supplies fallback behavior, and preserves existing data flow.

output_examples.input: Find the cause of repeated scrolling hitches in an Instruments trace.
output_examples.output: The analysis ranks hitch intervals, correlates main-thread activity, identifies expensive views, and traces likely invalidation sources.

best_practices: Provide deployment targets, relevant source files, and expected behavior before requesting changes.
Measure performance before and after each optimization with the same device, workload, and trace window.
Review availability gates, fallbacks, accessibility, localization, and tests before applying generated changes.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad architecture rewrites when a focused SwiftUI correction solves the problem.
Do not treat simulator traces as evidence for the unavailable SwiftUI Instruments lane.
Do not expose secrets through trace launch environment values or shared command logs.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SwiftUI development for iOS and macOS, including platform-specific views and scene behavior.

faq.question: Can it update deprecated SwiftUI APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify documented transitions and propose availability-gated replacements with suitable fallbacks.

faq.question: Does it require a specific architecture?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on data flow, correctness, testability, and performance without requiring MVVM or another architecture.

faq.question: Can it record Instruments traces?
faq.answer: Yes, on macOS with Xcode and xctrace available. Recording still requires an explicit target and appropriate device access.

faq.question: Can it analyze simulator traces?
faq.answer: Yes, but the simulator does not populate the SwiftUI lane. Use Time Profiler, Hangs, and Animation Hitches instead.

faq.question: Will it automatically edit my project?
faq.answer: No. The workflow edits code only when requested and expects project-specific builds and tests afterward.
